sentences.text: Ypupiara is an extinct genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil.
Based on preserved fossil measurements, Ypupiara is estimated to have reached about 2 to 3 meters in length when fully grown.
The only known species, Y. lopai, is known from a single specimen that was destroyed in a fire in 2018.
The holotype specimen DGM 921-R consists of a right maxilla and dentary associated with a fish jaw.
The holotype was destroyed in a fire at the National Museum of Brazil on September 2, 2018, shortly after photographs were taken.
The species name lopai honors the fossil's discoverer, Alberto Lopa.
Researchers suggest Ypupiara likely consumed fish significantly, based on its non-serrated conical teeth similar to other fish-eating animals.
It is hypothesized that Ypupiara preyed on smaller animals, mammals, reptiles, and fish.
Ypupiara is classified as the sister taxon to Austroraptor.
Ypupiara lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now South America.
